'''''The Martian''''' is a 2015 [[science fiction film|science fiction]] [[survival film]] directed by [[Ridley Scott]] from a screenplay by [[Drew Goddard]]. Based on [[Andy Weir]]'s [[The Martian (Weir novel)|2011 novel]], and distributed by [[20th Century Fox]], the film stars [[Matt Damon]], alongside an [[ensemble cast]] featuring [[Jessica Chastain]], [[Jeff Daniels]], [[Kristen Wiig]], [[Chiwetel Ejiofor]], [[Sean Bean]], [[Michael Peña]], [[Kate Mara]], [[Sebastian Stan]], and [[Mackenzie Davis]]. The film depicts an astronaut's struggle to survive on [[Mars]] after being left behind and [[NASA]]'s efforts to return him to Earth.

Producer [[Simon Kinberg]] began developing the film after Fox [[option (filmmaking)|optioned]] the novel in March 2013. Goddard, who adapted the novel into a screenplay, was initially attached to direct, but production was only approved after Scott replaced Goddard as director and Damon was cast as the main character. Filming began in November 2014 and lasted about 70 days, on a $108&nbsp;million budget. Twenty sets were built on one of the largest [[sound stage]]s in the world in [[Budapest]], Hungary. [[Wadi Rum]] in Jordan was also used for exterior filming.

''The Martian'' premiered at the [[2015 Toronto International Film Festival]] on September 11, 2015, and was released in the United Kingdom on September 30, and in the United States on October 2, in 2D, [[3D film|3D]], [[RealD 3D]], [[IMAX 3D]], and [[4DX]] formats.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/south-korea-box-office-martian-832932|title=South Korea Box Office: 'Martian' Dominates for Second Consecutive Week|last=Lee|first=Hyo-won|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|date=October 19, 2015|access-date=October 19, 2015|archive-date=November 8, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201108120041/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/south-korea-box-office-martian-832932|url-status=live}}</ref> The film opened to critical acclaim, and grossed $653.6&nbsp;million worldwide, becoming the [[2015 in film#Highest-grossing films|tenth-highest-grossing film of 2015]], as well as Scott's highest-grossing film to date. Named by the [[National Board of Review]] and by the [[American Film Institute]] one of the top-ten films of 2015, ''The Martian'' received [[List of accolades received by The Martian (film)|numerous accolades]], including seven nominations at the [[88th Academy Awards]].

==Plot==
[[File:PIA19913-MarsLandingSite-Ares3Mission-TheMartian-2015Film-20150517.jpg|thumb|left|Ares III mission landing site ([[Acidalia Planitia]] region)]]
In 2035, the crew of the Ares III [[human mission to Mars|mission to Mars]] is exploring [[Acidalia Planitia]] on [[Mars sol|Martian solar day]] (sol) 18 of their 31-sol expedition. A severe [[Climate of Mars#Dust storms|dust storm]] threatens their Mars Ascent Vehicle (MAV) and in the ensuing evacuation, astronaut Mark Watney is struck by flying debris and presumed dead. Facing imminent peril, the remaining crew takes off for their orbiting vessel, the ''Hermes'', which will then return them to Earth. Watney awakens after the storm, having narrowly survived his injuries. As he recovers within the crew's [[Mars habitat|surface habitat]] ("Hab"), he begins a video diary to document his thoughts on survival. Unable to communicate with Earth, his only chance of rescue is the next Mars mission in four years, when Ares IV will land at the [[Schiaparelli (Martian crater)|Schiaparelli crater]]. The Ares IV MAV has already arrived on the site in preparation for the mission. With this timeframe in mind, Watney's main survival concerns are food and travel. Being a [[botany|botanist]], he cultivates a potato garden inside the Hab using the crew's bio-waste with [[Martian soil]], and creates water from leftover rocket fuel. He also modifies a [[Space Exploration Vehicle|rover]] for the journey to Schiaparelli.

On Earth, [[NASA]] satellite planner Mindy Park notices Watney's activity from recorded satellite images, and suspects he must be alive. NASA director Teddy Sanders releases the news to the public but decides not to inform the Ares III crew en route to Earth, over [[Flight controller#Flight director|flight director]] Mitch Henderson's strong objection. Watney explores the surrounding terrain and studies his maps, but he quickly journeys out to retrieve the ''[[Mars Pathfinder|Pathfinder]]'' probe, hoping to restore its communications. Mars missions director Vincent Kapoor realizes this strategy, and quickly visits [[Jet Propulsion Laboratory]] (JPL) director Bruce Ng to use their replica of the probe. The agency makes contact with Watney and instructs him to link ''Pathfinder'' to the rover, where he can now communicate by text. With this breakthrough, Henderson is finally allowed to inform Watney's crewmates.

As Watney enters the Hab on one evening, a leak in the [[airlock]] causes an explosion that injures him and destroys the potato garden. Although he repairs the airlock, he is again threatened by starvation. NASA scrambles to procure a resupply ship for Watney, with Sanders ordering routine safety inspections bypassed to expedite the mission. This oversight results in catastrophe as the ship disintegrates shortly after launch. The [[China National Space Administration]] decides to offer a launch vehicle – originally intended for the ''Taiyang Shen'' space probe – to resupply Watney. Astrodynamicist Rich Purnell devises an alternative plan: send the ''Taiyang Shen'' launcher to resupply the ''Hermes'', which will then use Earth's gravity to "[[gravity assist|slingshot]]" back to Mars two years earlier than Ares IV. Sanders flatly rejects the idea, considering it too risky for the Ares III crew. Henderson surreptitiously sends the proposal to the crew, and they unanimously vote in favor and divert the ''Hermes''. Sanders is forced to support them publicly, but demands Henderson's resignation after the mission.

After waiting several months, Watney embarks on the long journey to the Ares IV MAV. He plans to use it to rendezvous with the ''Hermes'', but needs to lighten the load considerably by partially dismantling the cockpit. He takes off to orbit, but the ''Hermes'' crew find that they remain too far away and moving too fast to retrieve him. [[Commander]] Lewis quickly improvises to explode the airlock in part of the ship, resulting in air violently escaping and slowing them down. Lewis also pilots a tethered [[Manned Maneuvering Unit]] to personally reach Watney, but they are still too far apart. Watney quickly improvises by piercing his pressure suit, and propels himself with the escaping air, reaches Lewis, and manages to hold on. NASA and spectators across the world all celebrate the successful rescue.

After returning to Earth, Watney becomes a survival instructor for astronaut candidates. Five years later, as the Ares V is launching, those involved in Watney's rescue are seen in their current lives watching the launch footage.

Chastain prepared for her role by meeting with astronauts and scientists at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory and the [[Lyndon B. Johnson Space Center]]. She was inspired by astronaut [[Tracy Caldwell Dyson]], saying, "She's very matter of fact, very straightforward. My character is dealing with the guilt of leaving a crew member behind, but she's still responsible for the lives of five other crew mates. I tried to play her as Tracy would have been in those moments."<ref>{{cite news | last=Rottenberg | first=Josh | url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment/movies/la-ca-mn-sneaks-jessica-chastain-20150906-story.html | title=Heady days for Jessica Chastain as 'The Martian' and 'Crimson Peak' loom | work=[[Los Angeles Times]] | date=September 3, 2015 | access-date=October 2, 2015 | archive-date=August 2, 2020 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200802124152/https://www.latimes.com/entertainment/movies/la-ca-mn-sneaks-jessica-chastain-20150906-story.html | url-status=live }}</ref> Damon prepared for the role by a different method: "For me, the rehearsal process was sitting with Ridley and going kind of line-by-line and moment-by-moment through the script and playing out a plan of attack for what we wanted each scene to accomplish."<ref name="haricharan">{{cite news | author=Haricharan | url=https://bangaloremirror.indiatimes.com/entertainment/south-masala/Scott-made-The-Martian-really-easy-Matt-Damon/articleshow/49036039.cms | title=Scott made The Martian really easy: Matt Damon | work=[[Bangalore Mirror]] | date=September 20, 2015 | access-date=October 2, 2015 | archive-date=October 3, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151003212140/http://www.bangaloremirror.com/entertainment/south-masala/Scott-made-The-Martian-really-easy-Matt-Damon/articleshow/49036039.cms | url-status=live }}</ref>

The Media Action Network for Asian-Americans (MANAA) criticized the casting of white actress Mackenzie Davis as Mindy Park, whom it said author [[Andy Weir]] had described as Korean-American. The group also criticized the casting of Chiwetel Ejiofor as Vincent Kapoor, whom the organization said Weir described as an Asian Indian character. In the novel, the character's name was Venkat Kapoor, and he identifies religiously as a [[Hindu]] (a [[Baptist]] and a Hindu in the film). The group described these casting decisions as [[Racebending|whitewashing]], part of a broader phenomenon that deprives Asian actors of opportunities.<ref name=McNaryDave/> Weir said in October 2015 he perceived Mindy Park as Korean but said he did not explicitly write her as Korean. He also dismissed criticism of Ejiofor's casting, saying that Kapoor is "an American. Americans come from lots of different sources. You can be Venkat Kapoor and black."<ref name=MTV/> He said his novel intentionally avoided physical descriptions of his characters.<ref name=MTV/>

[[Naomi Scott]] was cast and filmed as Ryoko, a member of the JPL team. Her scenes were removed from the final cut.<ref>{{cite video|people=[[Jimmy Kimmel]] (host) [[Naomi Scott]] (guest)|title=Naomi Scott on Being in The Martian with Matt Damon |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JWo-gZGnqmM }} Clip from {{Cite episode |title=Dave Chappelle, Naomi Scott, Music from Weezer |url=http://abc.go.com/shows/jimmy-kimmel-live/episode-guide/2017-03/21-dave-chappelle-naomi-scott-weezer |access-date=April 30, 2017 |series=Jimmy Kimmel Live! |series-link=Jimmy Kimmel Live! |network=[[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]] |date=March 21, 2017 |season=15 |number=38 |archive-date=March 24, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170324043415/http://abc.go.com/shows/jimmy-kimmel-live/episode-guide/2017-03/21-dave-chappelle-naomi-scott-weezer |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Development===
''The Martian'' was directed by [[Ridley Scott]] and based on a screenplay by [[Drew Goddard]] that was adapted from Weir's 2011 [[The Martian (Weir novel)|novel of the same name]]. [[20th Century Fox]] [[option (filmmaking)|optioned]] the novel in March 2013, and producer [[Simon Kinberg]] was attached to develop the novel into a film.<ref>{{cite journal | last=Kroll | first=Justin | url=https://variety.com/2013/film/news/fox-finds-martian-for-simon-kinberg-exclusive-1200007238/ | title=Fox Finds 'Martian' For Simon Kinberg | journal=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] | date=March 12, 2013 | access-date=August 25, 2015 | archive-date=September 23, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923184234/https://variety.com/2013/film/news/fox-finds-martian-for-simon-kinberg-exclusive-1200007238/ | url-status=live }}</ref> The following May, Goddard entered negotiations with the studio to write and direct ''The Martian''.<ref>{{cite news | last=Sneider | first=Jeff | url=https://www.thewrap.com/drew-goddard-negotiations-write-direct-martian-fox-exclusive-91896/ | title=Drew Goddard in Negotiations to Write and Direct 'The Martian' for Fox | work=[[TheWrap]] | date=May 15, 2013 | access-date=August 25, 2015 | archive-date=January 6, 2017 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170106203548/http://www.thewrap.com/drew-goddard-negotiations-write-direct-martian-fox-exclusive-91896/ | url-status=live }}</ref> Goddard wrote a screenplay for the film<ref>{{cite news | last=Lidz | first=Gogo | url=http://www.newsweek.com/martian-matt-damon-ridley-scott-mars-343906 | title=Matt Damon Spills About 'The Martian' | work=[[Newsweek]] | date=June 18, 2015 | access-date=August 25, 2015 | archive-date=August 14, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150814012602/http://www.newsweek.com/martian-matt-damon-ridley-scott-mars-343906 | url-status=live }}</ref> and [[Matt Damon]] expressed interest in starring under Goddard's direction. Goddard then pursued an opportunity to direct ''Sinister Six'', a comic book film about [[Sinister Six|a team of supervillains]].<ref>{{cite news | last=Tilly | first=Chris | url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2015/06/17/matt-damon-explains-why-the-martian-is-a-love-letter-to-science | title=Matt Damon Explains Why The Martian is a Love Letter to Science | publisher=[[IGN]] | date=June 17, 2015 | access-date=August 26, 2015 | archive-date=August 24, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150824000333/http://www.ign.com/articles/2015/06/17/matt-damon-explains-why-the-martian-is-a-love-letter-to-science | url-status=live }}</ref> Kinberg then brought the book to Scott's attention.<ref>{{cite journal | last=Kroll | first=Justin | url=https://variety.com/2014/film/news/michael-pena-the-martian-matt-damon-ridley-scott-1201307660/ | title=Michael Pena Circles Ridley Scott's 'The Martian' With Matt Damon | journal=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] | date=September 24, 2014 | access-date=August 26, 2015 | archive-date=October 3, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151003092753/https://variety.com/2014/film/news/michael-pena-the-martian-matt-damon-ridley-scott-1201307660/ | url-status=live }}</ref>

In May 2014, Scott entered negotiations with the studio to direct the film with Damon cast as the film's stranded astronaut.<ref>{{cite journal | last=Kroll | first=Justin | url=https://variety.com/2014/film/news/ridley-scott-in-talks-to-direct-foxs-the-martian-with-matt-damon-1201180062/ | title=Ridley Scott in Talks to Direct Fox's 'The Martian' With Matt Damon | journal=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] | date=May 13, 2014 | access-date=August 25, 2015 | archive-date=August 31, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150831113743/http://variety.com/2014/film/news/ridley-scott-in-talks-to-direct-foxs-the-martian-with-matt-damon-1201180062/ | url-status=dead }}</ref> Scott said he was attracted by the emphasis on science and thought a balance could be struck between entertainment and learning. Damon said he was attracted by the novel, the screenplay, and the opportunity to work with Scott.<ref>{{cite news | last=White | first=James | url=https://www.empireonline.com/features/the-martian-at-NASA | title=Inside The Martian: Empire Meets NASA | work=[[Empire (magazine)|Empire]] | date=August 2015 | access-date=September 1, 2015 | archive-date=September 5, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150905055006/http://www.empireonline.com/features/the-martian-at-NASA | url-status=live }}</ref> Following Scott's commitment, the project picked up the pace and was quickly approved.<ref>{{cite journal | last=Kroll | first=Justin | url=https://variety.com/2014/film/news/jessica-chastain-to-joins-matt-damon-in-ridley-scotts-the-martian-1201214554/ | title=Jessica Chastain Joins Matt Damon in Ridley Scott's 'The Martian' | journal=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] | date=September 3, 2014 | access-date=August 26, 2015 | archive-date=September 30, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150930104956/http://variety.com/2014/film/news/jessica-chastain-to-joins-matt-damon-in-ridley-scotts-the-martian-1201214554/ | url-status=live }}</ref> Goddard has since expressed that he felt Scott made a much better film than he could have directed, telling ''Creative Screenwriting'', "When it's Scott, collaboration is easy because I just revere him. Every day I would just look around and think, 'Is that really Ridley Scott sitting there at the table? This is exciting!{{' "}}<ref>{{cite web|url=http://creativescreenwriting.com/life-goes-on-drew-goddard-on-the-martian/|title=Life Goes On: Drew Goddard on The Martian|last=McKittrick|first=Christopher|date=August 20, 2015|publisher=Creative Screenwriting|access-date=August 20, 2015|archive-date=January 9, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160109053739/http://creativescreenwriting.com/life-goes-on-drew-goddard-on-the-martian/|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Filming===
[[File:Wadi Rum in December.jpg|left|thumb|[[Wadi Rum]] in Jordan was used for external scenes on Mars in filming ''The Martian''.]]
[[Korda Studios]], a location {{convert|26|km|mi}} west of [[Budapest]], Hungary, in the wine-making village of [[Etyek]], was chosen for filming interior scenes of ''The Martian''. It had one of the largest [[sound stage]]s in the world.<ref>{{cite news | last=Daniels | first=Nia | url=http://www.kftv.com/news/2014/09/18/ridley-scotts-the-martian-sets-up-to-film-in-hungary | title=Ridley Scott's The Martian sets up to film in Hungary | publisher=KFTV | date=September 18, 2014 | access-date=August 26, 2015 | archive-date=July 22, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150722005251/http://www.kftv.com/news/2014/09/18/ridley-scotts-the-martian-sets-up-to-film-in-hungary | url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="weintraub">{{cite news | last=Weintraub | first=Steve | url=https://collider.com/the-martian-set-visit-30-things-to-know/ | title=Over 30 Things to Know About Ridley Scott's ''The Martian'' from our Budapest Set Visit | publisher=Collider.com | date=June 17, 2015 | access-date=August 26, 2015 | archive-date=December 5, 2020 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201205130524/https://collider.com/the-martian-set-visit-30-things-to-know/ | url-status=live }}</ref> Filming began in Hungary on November 24, 2014.<ref>{{cite journal | last=Foundas | first=Scott | url=https://variety.com/2014/film/news/ridley-scott-exodus-gods-and-kings-christian-bale-1201363668/ | title='Exodus: Gods and Kings' Director Ridley Scott on Creating His Vision of Moses | journal=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] | date=November 25, 2014 | access-date=August 26, 2015 | archive-date=September 5, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150905211836/https://variety.com/2014/film/news/ridley-scott-exodus-gods-and-kings-christian-bale-1201363668/ | url-status=live }}</ref> Around 20 sets were constructed for the film, which was filmed with 3D cameras.<ref name="weintraub" /> Actual potatoes were grown in a sound stage next to the one used for filming. They were planted at different times so that different stages of growth could be shown in film scenes.<ref name="klimek">{{cite journal | last=Klimek | first=Chris | url=http://www.airspacemag.com/daily-planet/matt-damon-first-farmer-mars-180956410/ | title=Matt Damon, First Farmer on Mars | journal=[[Air & Space/Smithsonian|Air & Space]] | date=August 28, 2015 | access-date=September 1, 2015 | archive-date=May 23, 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160523214205/http://www.airspacemag.com/daily-planet/matt-damon-first-farmer-mars-180956410/ | url-status=live }}</ref> A team of six people built 15 suits for the film. External scenes depicting Mars were filmed in [[Wadi Rum]], a [[UNESCO]] world heritage site in [[Jordan]], over eight days in March 2015.<ref name="weintraub" /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.jordantimes.com/news/local/ridley-scott-hany-abu-asad-shoot-their-latest-movies-jordan|title=Ridley Scott, Hany Abu Asad shoot their latest movies in Jordan|work=Jordan Times |date=March 16, 2015|access-date=October 25, 2016|archive-date=September 24, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200924145946/http://www.jordantimes.com/news/local/ridley-scott-hany-abu-asad-shoot-their-latest-movies-jordan|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sponsored/travel/jordan-places-to-visit/11888487/wadi-rum-desert-tours.html|title=Wadi Rum: a mesmerising desert guarded by stone giants|access-date=October 8, 2015|date=October 1, 2015|work=The Daily Telegraph|archive-date=September 20, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200920213443/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sponsored/travel/jordan-places-to-visit/11888487/wadi-rum-desert-tours.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Wadi Rum had been used as a location for other films set on Mars, including ''[[Mission to Mars]]'' (2000), ''[[Red Planet (film)|Red Planet]]'' (2000) and ''[[The Last Days on Mars]]'' (2013).<ref>{{cite news | author=Staff | url=http://www.albawaba.com/entertainment/that's-a-wrap!-hollywood's-%22the-martian%22-and-palestine's-%22arab-idol%22-in-jordan-670308 | title=That's a wrap! Hollywood's 'The Martian' and Palestine's 'Arab Idol' finish scenes in Jordan | work=[[The Jordan Times]] | date=March 17, 2015 | access-date=August 26, 2015 | archive-date=October 27, 2020 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201027043549/https://www.albawaba.com/entertainment/that%27s-a-wrap%21-hollywood%27s-%22the-martian%22-and-palestine%27s-%22arab-idol%22-in-jordan-670308 | url-status=live }}</ref> All told, filming lasted about 70 days.<ref name="weintraub" />
A special Mars rover model was built for the filming; the film cast and team presented the rover model to Jordan in return for the hospitality they had received. The rover is now exhibited in Jordan's [[Royal Automobile Museum]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://ameinfo.com/media-and-marketing/media/cinema/the-royal-automobile-museum-patrons-the-premiere-of-the-martian-film/#sthash.eoBeIKI4.dpuf|access-date=October 22, 2015|date=October 22, 2015|title=The Royal Automobile Museum patrons the premiere of 'The Martian' film|work=ameinfo|publisher=Mediaquest Corp.|archive-date=September 24, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200924155026/https://www.ameinfo.com/media-and-marketing/media/cinema/the-royal-automobile-museum-patrons-the-premiere-of-the-martian-film/#sthash.eoBeIKI4.dpuf|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://edition.cnn.com/2015/10/02/entertainment/the-martian-review-thr/|title=Review: 'The Martian' is a pleasure|access-date=October 8, 2015|date=October 5, 2015|publisher=[[CNN]]|archive-date=February 17, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200217162315/https://edition.cnn.com/2015/10/02/entertainment/the-martian-review-thr/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Weir avoided writing Watney as lonely and depressed in his novel. While Watney's humor is preserved in the film, Scott also depicted the character's isolation in the vast, dusty Martian landscape. [[Todd McCarthy]] of ''[[The Hollywood Reporter]]'' wrote: "The scenes back on Earth provide a hectic, densely populated counterweight to the Martian aridity, which is magnificently represented by exteriors shot in the vicinity of Wadi Rum in Jordan."<ref>{{cite news|last=McCarthy|first=Todd|title='The Martian': TIFF Review|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/review/martian-tiff-review-820882|access-date=May 30, 2016|work=The Hollywood Reporter|date=September 11, 2015|archive-date=October 15, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151015185753/http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/movie/martian/review/820882|url-status=live}}</ref> Damon said he and Scott were inspired by the documentary film ''[[Touching the Void (film)|Touching the Void]]'' (2003), which featured trapped mountain climbers.<ref name="hutchinson">{{cite news | last=Hutchinson | first=Lee | url=https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2015/08/ars-talks-with-matt-damon-on-being-astronaut-mark-watney-in-the-martian/ | title=Ars talks with Matt Damon on being astronaut Mark Watney in ''The Martian'' | website=[[Ars Technica]] | date=August 27, 2015 | access-date=September 1, 2015 | archive-date=August 30, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150830235121/http://arstechnica.com/the-multiverse/2015/08/ars-talks-with-matt-damon-on-being-astronaut-mark-watney-in-the-martian/ | url-status=live }}</ref> Scott also expected to film Watney as a [[Robinson Crusoe]], a character in full isolation, but learned to film Watney differently since the character would be self-monitoring his behavior under the watch of various mission cameras.<ref name="klimek" />

According to Scott, the first cut of the film was 2 hours and 45 minutes long.<ref>{{cite news|title=Ridley Scott Talks 'The Martian' Extended Cut and More|url=https://collider.com/ridley-scott-talks-the-martian-extended-cut-deleted-scenes-and-more/|access-date=June 28, 2016|date=September 28, 2015|archive-date=July 2, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160702190906/http://collider.com/ridley-scott-talks-the-martian-extended-cut-deleted-scenes-and-more/|url-status=live}}</ref> An extended cut of the film was released on home video.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.movie-censorship.com/news.php?ID=9539 |title=The Martian – Ridley Scott Confirms Extended Cut |date=September 23, 2015 |first=Gerald |last=Wurm |publisher=Movie-Censorship.com |access-date=January 5, 2016 |archive-date=January 7, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160107215041/http://www.movie-censorship.com/news.php?ID=9539 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Collider">{{cite news|title=The Martian Extended Cut Has 10 Minutes of New Footage|url=https://collider.com/the-martian-extended-edition-details/|access-date=May 28, 2016|work=Collider|date=April 30, 2016|archive-date=June 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160604060252/http://collider.com/the-martian-extended-edition-details/|url-status=live}}</ref>

===NASA involvement===
[[File:NASA Journey to Mars and “The Martian" (201508180009HQ).jpg|thumb|right|Damon while making hand prints in concrete at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory. He is accompanied by Jim Erickson (left) and [[Andrew J. Feustel]] (right).]]
When the novel was first published, [[NASA]] invited Weir to tour the Johnson Space Center and Jet Propulsion Laboratory. When Scott began preparing the film, Weir contacted NASA to collaborate on the film.<ref name="bradley">{{cite news | last=Bradley | first=Ryan | url=http://www.popsci.com/why-nasa-helped-ridley-scott-create-martian-film-and-what-means-future-sci-fi-space-movies | title=Why NASA Helped Ridley Scott Create 'The Martian' Film | work=[[Popular Science]] | date=August 19, 2015 | access-date=August 28, 2015 | archive-date=August 31, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150831072945/http://www.popsci.com/why-nasa-helped-ridley-scott-create-martian-film-and-what-means-future-sci-fi-space-movies | url-status=live }}</ref> When Scott and producer [[Mark Huffam]] had their first production meeting, they called NASA and spoke with its film and television liaison Bert Ulrich.<ref name="lidz">{{cite journal | last=Lidz | first=Gogo | url=http://www.newsweek.com/2015/10/02/why-nasa-faked-mars-landing-374214.html | title=NASA and 'The Martian': It Was Written in the Stars | journal=[[Newsweek]] | date=September 20, 2015 | access-date=October 2, 2015 | archive-date=October 3, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151003154645/http://www.newsweek.com/2015/10/02/why-nasa-faked-mars-landing-374214.html | url-status=live }}</ref> NASA decided to help the filmmakers with depicting the science and technology in ''The Martian'' since it saw potential in promoting space exploration.<ref name="bradley"/>

NASA staff members that joined the effort included [[James L. Green]], director of the [[Planetary Science Division]], and [[Dave Lavery]], program executive for Solar System Exploration.<ref name="lidz" /> Scott conversed with Green twice before filming started. During one month, NASA answered hundreds of questions on radioisotope systems, the look of potential "habs"—the residences for future Mars astronauts—and more. The questions were answered by Green or passed on to the right expert, and then came back to Scott's team to make their way into the production.<ref name="latimes">{{cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment/movies/moviesnow/la-et-mn-the-martian-movie-mars-water-matt-damon-20150929-story.html|title=For Matt Damon movie 'The Martian,' lots of research – and a watery coincidence|first=Steven|last=Zeitchik|work=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=September 29, 2015|access-date=October 2, 2015|archive-date=October 2, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151002021456/http://www.latimes.com/entertainment/movies/moviesnow/la-et-mn-the-martian-movie-mars-water-matt-damon-20150929-story.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="wall">{{cite news | last=Wall | first=Mike | url=http://www.space.com/30327-the-martian-movie-nasa-photos.html | title='The Martian' Lands at NASA's Mars Mission Control (Photos) | publisher=[[Space.com]] | date=August 20, 2015 | access-date=August 28, 2015 | archive-date=August 24, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150824153832/http://www.space.com/30327-the-martian-movie-nasa-photos.html | url-status=live }}</ref> The space agency also provided hundreds of real images of Mars and control centers, down to what the computer screens look like.<ref name="nasa" /> Green arranged an eight-hour tour of the Johnson Space Center in [[Houston]] for production designer [[Arthur Max]], who met with specialists and took hundreds of photos.<ref name="latimes" /><ref name="nasa" /> The production designer created a futuristic, heavily modernized Mission Control as a studio set; ''[[Ars Technica]]'' described its depiction as "the space agency that we all dream of" and the opposite of the real Johnson Center's appearance as "a run down college campus".<ref name="The Martian brings science, largely unchanged, from book to screen">{{cite web |last=Hutchinson |first=Lee |title=The Martian brings science, largely unchanged, from book to screen |url=https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2015/09/the-martian-brings-science-largely-unchanged-from-book-to-screen/ |website=[[Ars Technica]] |date=September 12, 2015 |access-date=October 4, 2015 |archive-date=October 2, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151002225202/http://arstechnica.com/the-multiverse/2015/09/the-martian-brings-science-largely-unchanged-from-book-to-screen/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

''[[Newsweek]]'' said NASA collaborated more with ''The Martian'' than most other space-themed films: "Staff from many NASA departments consulted on the film, from script development through principal photography, and are now helping with marketing timed to the theatrical release."<ref name="lidz" /> As part of the collaboration, the production's NASA liaison included the front page of the script for the film in the payload of the spacecraft [[Orion (spacecraft)|Orion]] during its [[Exploration Flight Test 1]] on December 5, 2014.<ref>{{cite magazine | last=Vilkomerson | first=Sara | url=https://www.ew.com/article/2014/12/19/ridley-scott-martian-script-into-space | title=Ridley Scott sends his 'Martian' script into space | magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]] | date=December 19, 2014 | access-date=September 1, 2015 | archive-date=August 23, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150823072742/http://www.ew.com/article/2014/12/19/ridley-scott-martian-script-into-space | url-status=live }}</ref>

The ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'' said NASA and the wider scientific community anticipated the film as a way to publicize a [[human mission to Mars]]. The ''New York Times'' reports that the film "serves as a nice plug for NASA, which has returned the favor by pushing the movie on its website. (On Monday [September 28, 2015], scientists announced that signs of liquid water could be seen in photographs taken on Mars by a camera on the [[Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter]],<ref name="NASA-20150928">{{cite web |last1=Webster |first1=Guy |last2=Agle |first2=DC |last3=Brown |first3=Dwayne |last4=Cantillo |first4=Laurie |title=NASA Confirms Evidence That Liquid Water Flows on Today's Mars |url=http://www.jpl.nasa.gov/news/news.php?feature=4722 |date=28 September 2015 |publisher=[[NASA]] |access-date=28 September 2015 |archive-date=September 29, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150929121338/http://www.jpl.nasa.gov/news/news.php?feature=4722 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="NYT-20150928">{{cite news |last=Chang |first=Kenneth |title=NASA Says Signs of Liquid Water Flowing on Mars |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2015/09/29/science/space/mars-life-liquid-water.html |date=28 September 2015 |work=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=28 September 2015 |archive-date=August 8, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190808103911/https://www.nytimes.com/2015/09/29/science/space/mars-life-liquid-water.html |url-status=live }}</ref> timing that suggests NASA certainly has the whole cross-promotion thing down.)"<ref name="NYT-20151001" /> Jim Erickson, NASA project manager, said the film would show moviegoers "the risks and rewards" of humans traveling to Mars.<ref name="dave">{{cite news | last=Dave | first=Paresh | url=https://www.latimes.com/science/la-fi-martian-movie-science-20150820-story.html | title=Why NASA scientists are excited about Matt Damon film 'The Martian' | work=[[Los Angeles Times]] | date=August 19, 2015 | access-date=September 1, 2015 | archive-date=September 5, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150905234359/http://www.latimes.com/science/la-fi-martian-movie-science-20150820-story.html | url-status=live }}</ref>

In October 2015, NASA presented a new web tool to follow Watney's trek across Mars<ref name="NASA-20151008b">{{cite web |last=Gipson |first=Lillian |title=Follow Mark Watney's Epic Trek on Mars with New NASA Web Tool |url=http://www.nasa.gov/feature/follow-mark-watney-s-epic-trek-on-mars-with-new-nasa-web-tool |date=October 8, 2015 |publisher=[[NASA]] |access-date=October 29, 2015 |archive-date=October 9, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151009171916/http://www.nasa.gov/feature/follow-mark-watney-s-epic-trek-on-mars-with-new-nasa-web-tool |url-status=live }}</ref> and details of NASA's next steps, as well as a [[Effect of spaceflight on the human body|health hazards report]]<ref name="AP-20151029">{{cite news |last=Dunn |first=Marcia |title=Report: NASA needs better handle on health hazards for Mars |url=http://apnews.excite.com/article/20151029/us-sci-space-travel-health-6dfd5b2c76.html |date=October 29, 2015 |work=[[AP News]] |access-date=October 30, 2015 |archive-date=January 30, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190130041700/http://apnews.excite.com/article/20151029/us-sci-space-travel-health-6dfd5b2c76.html |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="NASA-20151029oig">{{cite web |author=Staff |title=NASA's Efforts to Manage Health and Human Performance Risks for Space Exploration (IG-16-003) |url=https://oig.nasa.gov/audits/reports/FY16/IG-16-003.pdf |date=October 29, 2015 |work=[[NASA]] |access-date=October 29, 2015 |archive-date=April 5, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160405072459/https://oig.nasa.gov/audits/reports/FY16/IG-16-003.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref> for a real-world [[Human mission to Mars|human journey to Mars]].<ref name="NASA-20151008">{{cite web |title= REPORT: NASA's Pioneering Next Steps in Space Exploration |url= http://www.nasa.gov/sites/default/files/atoms/files/journey-to-mars-next-steps-20151008_508.pdf |date= October 8, 2015 |publisher= [[NASA]] |access-date= October 29, 2015 |archive-date= October 11, 2015 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20151011075743/http://www.nasa.gov/sites/default/files/atoms/files/journey-to-mars-next-steps-20151008_508.pdf |url-status= live }}</ref><ref name="CAP-20151028">{{cite web |author=Staff |title=Human Space Exploration: The Next Steps |url=https://www.americanprogress.org/events/2015/10/19/123515/human-space-exploration-the-next-steps/ |date=October 28, 2015 |publisher=[[Center for American Progress]] |access-date=October 29, 2015 |archive-date=August 19, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190819032401/https://www.americanprogress.org/events/2015/10/19/123515/human-space-exploration-the-next-steps/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Video-20151028">{{cite web |author=Staff |title=NASA: "Human Space Exploration – The Next Steps" – Video (55:48) |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Bem-Lqsg_9U |publisher=[[Center for American Progress]] |date=October 28, 2015 |access-date=October 29, 2015 |archive-date=January 6, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160106192720/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Bem-Lqsg_9U |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2016, then-US President [[Barack Obama]] named ''The Martian'' as among the best science fiction films he had ever seen.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.pbs.org/newshour/nation/heres-list-president-obamas-favorite-sci-fi-movies |title=Here's a list of President Obama's favorite sci-fi movies |work=[[PBS Newshour]] |date=October 13, 2016 |access-date=October 13, 2016 |agency=Associated Press |archive-date=October 13, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161013221928/http://www.pbs.org/newshour/rundown/heres-list-president-obamas-favorite-sci-fi-movies/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Music==
{{Main|The Martian (soundtrack){{!}}''The Martian'' (soundtrack)}}
[[Harry Gregson-Williams]] composed the [[film score|score]] for ''The Martian''. It is the fourth collaboration between Gregson-Williams and Scott. Gregson-Williams previously worked on music for Scott's films ''[[Kingdom of Heaven (film)|Kingdom of Heaven]]'' (2005), ''[[Prometheus (2012 film)|Prometheus]]'' (2012) and ''[[Exodus: Gods and Kings]]'', composing the main film score for the first and last films, and doing additional music for the other two.<ref name="music">{{cite web|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/martian-composer-creating-matt-damons-828847|title='The Martian' Composer on Creating Matt Damon's Theme, Ridley Scott's 'Prometheus' Plans|first=Ryan|last=Gajewski|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|date=October 3, 2015|access-date=October 4, 2015|archive-date=October 5, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151005091636/http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/martian-composer-creating-matt-damons-828847|url-status=live}}</ref>

A running gag in the film is commander Melissa Lewis' love for 1970s songs (especially of the [[disco]] genre, which apparently Watney hates), the only music available to Watney on Mars which often appears as [[diegetic music]]. The soundtrack includes:<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/songs-from-the-martian-and-original-motion-picture-score-by-harry-gregson-williams-available-digitally-today-300153292.html|title="Songs From The Martian" and "Original Motion Picture Score" by Harry Gregson-Williams Available Digitally Today|agency=[[PR Newswire]]|date=October 2, 2015|access-date=October 4, 2015|archive-date=October 5, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151005044302/http://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/songs-from-the-martian-and-original-motion-picture-score-by-harry-gregson-williams-available-digitally-today-300153292.html|url-status=live}}</ref>
* "[[Turn the Beat Around]]" by [[Vicki Sue Robinson]]
* "[[Hot Stuff (Donna Summer song)|Hot Stuff]]" by [[Donna Summer]]
* "[[Rock the Boat (The Hues Corporation song)|Rock the Boat]]" by [[The Hues Corporation]]
* "[[Don't Leave Me This Way]]" by [[Thelma Houston]]
* "[[Starman (song)|Starman]]" by [[David Bowie]]
* "[[Waterloo (ABBA song)|Waterloo]]" by [[ABBA]]
* "[[Love Train]]" by [[The O'Jays]]
* "[[I Will Survive]]" by [[Gloria Gaynor]] ([[closing credits]])

The exit music, which includes "Don't Leave Me This Way" and "I Will Survive," is a commentary on Watney's situation on Mars.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/lifestyle/style/the-martian-has-a-killer-soundtrack--here-are-the-5-best-musical-moments/2015/10/05/313e6008-6b8a-11e5-aa5b-f78a98956699_story.html |title='The Martian' has a killer soundtrack – here are the 5 best musical moments |first=Emily |last=Yahr |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |date=October 5, 2015 |access-date=March 26, 2018 |archive-date=August 13, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180813044448/https://www.washingtonpost.com/lifestyle/style/the-martian-has-a-killer-soundtrack--here-are-the-5-best-musical-moments/2015/10/05/313e6008-6b8a-11e5-aa5b-f78a98956699_story.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Marketing==
[[20th Century Fox]] launched a [[viral marketing]] campaign for ''The Martian''.<ref name="lesnick">{{cite news | last=Lesnick | first=Simon | url=https://www.comingsoon.net/movies/trailers/476609-neil-degrasse-tyson-hosts-the-martian-viral-video | title=Neil deGrasse Tyson Hosts The Martian Viral Video | publisher=ComingSoon.net | date=August 27, 2015 | access-date=August 28, 2015 | archive-date=August 29, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150829192657/http://www.comingsoon.net/movies/trailers/476609-neil-degrasse-tyson-hosts-the-martian-viral-video | url-status=live }}</ref> On June 7, 2015, NASA astronaut [[Michael J. Massimino]] shared an in-universe [[video blog|video diary]] depicting Damon's character and the other crew members.<ref>{{cite magazine | last=Rosen | first=Christopher | url=https://www.ew.com/article/2015/06/07/martian-promo-matt-damon | title=Matt Damon says farewell to Earth in viral promo for 'The Martian' | magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]] | date=June 7, 2015 | access-date=August 28, 2015 | archive-date=August 23, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150823154126/http://www.ew.com/article/2015/06/07/martian-promo-matt-damon | url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite AV media |title=Ares 3: Farewell |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CumZP6_9sHU |website=ARES: live YouTube Channel |publisher=20th Century FOX |access-date=June 10, 2015 }}{{dead link|date=December 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GMP9WI9N0Hc |title=The Martian Ares 3 Farewell |date=September 13, 2015 |publisher=20th Century Studios NZ |via=YouTube}}</ref> ''[[Ars Technica]]'' compared the video diary to similar viral videos marketed for Scott's 2012 film ''Prometheus'' in having a similar "style of slickly produced fictional promotional material". The marketing video was awarded two [[2016 Webby Awards|Webby Awards in 2016]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://winners.webbyawards.com/2016/video/general-video/drama-individual-short-or-episode/161584/the-martian-ares-3-farewell |title=The Martian - “Ares 3 Farewell” |publisher=Webby Awards}}</ref> The studio then released an official trailer on June 8.<ref>{{cite news | last=Hutchinson | first=Lee | url=https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2015/06/first-teaser-for-the-martian-movie-released-with-mark-watney-and-friends/ | title=First trailers for ''The Martian'' movie released, with Mark Watney and friends | work=[[Ars Technica]] | date=June 8, 2015 | access-date=August 28, 2015 | archive-date=August 17, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150817012330/http://arstechnica.com/the-multiverse/2015/06/first-teaser-for-the-martian-movie-released-with-mark-watney-and-friends/ | url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[Forbes]]'' said, "20th Century Fox has cut together a pretty perfect trailer in that it absolutely makes the sale. It establishes the stakes, offers a sympathetic lead character, shows off an all-star cast, tosses out a potential catchphrase, and ends on a grimly humorous tagline."<ref>{{cite news | last=Mendelson | first=Scott | url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/scottmendelson/2015/06/08/trailer-talk-matt-damon-jessica-chastains-the-martian-aces-marketing-101/ | title=Trailer Talk: Matt Damon, Jessica Chastain's 'The Martian' Aces Marketing 101 | work=[[Forbes]] | date=June 8, 2015 | access-date=August 28, 2015 | archive-date=August 2, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150802201440/http://www.forbes.com/sites/scottmendelson/2015/06/08/trailer-talk-matt-damon-jessica-chastains-the-martian-aces-marketing-101/ | url-status=live }}</ref> In response to the trailer, [[Jimmy Kimmel]], host of the late-night talk show ''[[Jimmy Kimmel Live!]]'', released a spoof trailer, ''The Mastronaut: Emission to Mars'', that edited the original to parody the film.<ref>{{cite news | last=Lee | first=Ashley | url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/jimmy-kimmel-airs-martian-trailer-802101 | title=Jimmy Kimmel Airs 'The Martian' Trailer Spoof to Make Fun of Matt Damon | work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] | date=June 12, 2015 | access-date=August 28, 2015 | archive-date=August 23, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150823183350/http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/live-feed/jimmy-kimmel-airs-martian-trailer-802101 | url-status=live }}</ref>

At the start of August, Fox released another video, depicting interviews with each of the main crew members.<ref>{{cite news | last=Baker-Whitelaw | first=Gavia | url=http://www.dailydot.com/geek/the-martian-viral-matt-damon-cast/ | title=New viral video for 'The Martian' shows how the Ares crew deals with isolation | work=[[The Daily Dot]] | date=August 4, 2015 | access-date=August 28, 2015 | archive-date=September 23, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923225955/http://www.dailydot.com/geek/the-martian-viral-matt-damon-cast/ | url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YVD_EE2ugzI |title=The Martian {{!}} The Right Stuff {{!}} Web Exclusive 2015 |date=August 4, 2015 |publisher=20th Century Studios UK |via=YouTube}}</ref> Mid-month, the studio released another film trailer, and NASA hosted a "Martian Day" at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory to both promote ''The Martian'' and highlight the space program's ongoing efforts to carry out a [[human mission to Mars]].<ref name="wall" /> At the end of August, Fox released another video, presenting it as a special episode of the TV series ''[[StarTalk (2015 TV series)|StarTalk]]'' in which astrophysicist [[Neil deGrasse Tyson]] discusses the hazards of traveling to Mars.<ref>{{cite news | last=Bradley | first=Laura | url=http://www.slate.com/blogs/browbeat/2015/08/28/neil_degrasse_tyson_explains_ridley_scott_s_the_martian_s_science_video.html | title=Neil deGrasse Tyson Soothingly Explains the Science Behind ''The Martian'' | work=Slate | date=August 28, 2015 | access-date=September 1, 2015 | archive-date=August 30, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150830235742/http://www.slate.com/blogs/browbeat/2015/08/28/neil_degrasse_tyson_explains_ridley_scott_s_the_martian_s_science_video.html | url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C0cWlxB9kqk |title=The Martian Featurette Ares Our Greatest Adventure |date=September 13, 2015 |publisher=20th Century Studios NZ |via=YouTube}}</ref> In September, Scott's RSA Films released a teaser for ''The Martian'' that depicted Damon wearing [[Under Armour]] sports clothing and being active in his off-world tasks.<ref name="diaz">{{cite news | last=Diaz | first=Ann-Christine | url=http://creativity-online.com/work/the-martian-leave-your-mark/43187 | title=Matt Damon Works Out in Under Armour in Teaser for Ridley Scott's 'The Martian' | work=[[Creativity (magazine)|Creativity]] | date=September 9, 2015 | access-date=October 2, 2015 | archive-date=October 2, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151002052301/http://creativity-online.com/work/the-martian-leave-your-mark/43187 | url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RMgYTNGpT9Y |title=The Martian {{!}} Leave Your Mark {{!}} Web Exclusive HD |date=September 9, 2015 |publisher=20th Century Studios UK |via=YouTube}}</ref> The teaser originated from a collaboration between RSA Films and the marketing shop 3{{sic|hide=y|A|M}} (the theatrical advertising arm of the agency Wild Card), initiated in 2014, to produce advertising content for ''The Martian''. RSA contacted the advertising agency [[Droga5]], under whom Under Armour is a client.<ref name="beer">{{cite news | last=Beer | first=Jeff | url=http://www.fastcocreate.com/3050858/why-the-new-teaser-for-the-martian-is-also-an-under-armour-ad | title=Why The New Teaser For 'The Martian' Is Also An Under Armour Ad | work=[[Fast Company (magazine)|Fast Company]] | date=September 9, 2015 | access-date=October 2, 2015 | archive-date=October 3, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151003170449/http://www.fastcocreate.com/3050858/why-the-new-teaser-for-the-martian-is-also-an-under-armour-ad | url-status=dead }}</ref> Droga5 ultimately collaborated with [[William Morris Endeavor|WME]] and 3{{sic|hide=y|A|M}} to produce the teaser.<ref name="diaz" />

NASA participated in the marketing of the film despite its lack of involvement with previous films. Though it turned down a request for ''[[Interstellar (film)|Interstellar]]'' to be screened on the ISS,<ref name="nasa">{{cite web|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/how-nasa-kept-things-real-828130|title=How NASA Kept Things Real With 'The Martian'|first=Pamela|last=McClintock|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|date=September 30, 2015|access-date=October 2, 2015|archive-date=October 3, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151003050143/http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/how-nasa-kept-things-real-828130|url-status=live}}</ref> ''The Martian'' was screened on board<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/aponline/2015/09/29/world/ap-us-film-the-martian.html/|title=Damon, Scott Book a Return to Space in 'The Martian'|agency=Associated Press|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=September 29, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151002072155/https://www.nytimes.com/aponline/2015/09/29/world/ap-us-film-the-martian.html/|access-date=October 28, 2020|archive-date=October 2, 2015}}</ref> 402&nbsp;km (250 miles) above the Earth's surface on September 19, 2015, and also at the Johnson Space Center in Houston, and at the [[Kennedy Space Center]] at [[Cape Canaveral]] on October 1, 2015.<ref name="nasa"/>

In November 2015, 20th Century Fox announced ''The Martian VR Experience'', a "virtual reality adventure" where viewers play as Mark Watney and reenact scenes from the film.<ref>{{Cite web|last1=Ewalt |first1=David M. |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/davidewalt/2015/11/20/fox-returns-to-the-red-planet-in-the-martian-vr-experience/#30f483e07aca|title=Fox Releases Sneak Peek Of 'The Martian VR Experience'|website=Forbes|access-date=March 27, 2016|archive-date=April 9, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160409121015/http://www.forbes.com/sites/davidewalt/2015/11/20/fox-returns-to-the-red-planet-in-the-martian-vr-experience/#30f483e07aca|url-status=live}}</ref> The project was executive produced by Scott alongside Joel Newton and directed by [[Robert Stromberg]]. It was released for [[HTC Vive]] and [[PlayStation VR]] on November 15, 2016, and is also available for the [[Oculus Rift]] and [[Samsung Gear VR]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theverge.com/2016/11/14/13621466/the-martian-vr-experience-launch-sony-playstation-vr-htc-vive|title=The Martian VR Experience is coming to PSVR and Vive tomorrow|last=Robertson|first=Adi|date=November 14, 2016|website=The Verge|access-date=February 11, 2017|archive-date=February 12, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170212163956/http://www.theverge.com/2016/11/14/13621466/the-martian-vr-experience-launch-sony-playstation-vr-htc-vive|url-status=live}}</ref> The project won 2 major awards; a [[Silver Lion]] at the [[Cannes Film Festival]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.robertstromberg.com/the-martian-vr-experience |title=The Martian VR Experience |first=Robert |last=Stromberg |website=robertstromberg.com}}</ref> and an AICP Award.

22, 2015 | access-date=October 1, 2015 | archive-date=October 4, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151004115853/http://www.ew.com/article/2015/09/22/the-martian-new-york-film-festival | url-status=live }}</ref> It also screened at [[Fantastic Fest]] in [[Austin, Texas]], on September 29, 2015.<ref>{{cite magazine | last=Collis | first=Clark | ===Box office forecast===
{{Anchor|Box office}}
Two months before ''The Martian''{{'}}s release, ''[[BoxOffice (magazine)|BoxOffice]]'' forecast that the film would gross {{nowrap|$46 million}} on its opening weekend in the United States and ultimately {{nowrap|$172 million}} in its theatrical run. The magazine said positive factors for its performance included the continued sales of Weir's novel, Scott's success with past science fiction films, and the positive reception of prior space-based films ''[[Gravity (2013 film)|Gravity]]'' (2013) and ''[[Interstellar (film)|Interstellar]]'' (2014). The magazine said negative factors included Damon not being a consistent draw at the box office, ''Gravity'' and ''Interstellar'' setting high expectations, and Scott's "stumble" with his previous film ''Exodus: Gods and Kings'' (2014).<ref>{{cite journal |author=Staff |url=http://pro.boxoffice.com/featured_stories/2015-08-long-range-forecast-the-martian |title=Long Range Forecast: 'The Martian' |journal=[[BoxOffice (magazine)|BoxOffice]] |date=August 7, 2015 |access-date=October 2, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150913002510/http://pro.boxoffice.com/featured_stories/2015-08-long-range-forecast-the-martian |archive-date=September 13, 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref> A week before the film's release, pre-release trackings in North America (United States and Canada) showed that the film was on pace to earn between $40–50&nbsp;million at its opening weekend from 3,826 theaters.<ref name="track1">{{cite web |url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/box-office-preview-martian-set-828003 |title=Box-Office Preview: 'Martian' Set to Rocket to No. 1; 'The Walk' Opens in Imax |first=Pamela |last=McClintock |work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] |date=September 29, 2015 |access-date=September 30, 2020 |archive-date=August 27, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200827205713/https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/box-office-preview-martian-set-828003 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In comparison to other contemporary space films, ''Gravity'', facing far less competition, opened to a better-than-expected $55.8&nbsp;million in 2013. In November 2014, ''Interstellar'' debuted to $47.5&nbsp;million.<ref name="track1" /> Unlike ''Gravity'' and ''Interstellar'', which had the benefit of IMAX locations, boosting profits, ''The Martian'' was not initially playing in IMAX, since IMAX was committed to an exclusive run of [[Robert Zemeckis]]' ''[[The Walk (2015 film)|The Walk]]''. ''The Martian'' played in more than 350 premium large-format theaters including 2,550 3D locations.<ref name="track1"/><ref name="track3">{{cite web |url=https://variety.com/2015/film/news/the-martian-box-office-pre-sales-gravity-1201606551/ |title='The Martian' Outselling 'Gravity' in Weekend Pre-Sales |first=Brent |last=Lang |work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |date=September 30, 2015 |access-date=October 1, 2015 |archive-date=October 1, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151001223759/http://variety.com/2015/film/news/the-martian-box-office-pre-sales-gravity-1201606551/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Also, the film was released several days after the announcement of NASA's discovery of [[water on Mars|water on Mars' planetary surface]],<ref name="NASA-20150928" /><ref name="NYT-20150928"/> which might have aided in boosting its opening.<ref name="track2">{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2015/09/the-martian-the-walk-sicario-box-office-preview-1201558104/|title='The Martian' Looks Forward To A Great Landing; 'The Walk' Begins To Run & 'Sicario' Ups Forces – Box Office Preview|first=Anthony|last=D'Alessandro|work=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|date=September 29, 2015|access-date=September 30, 2015|archive-date=September 30, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150930151343/https://deadline.com/2015/09/the-martian-the-walk-sicario-box-office-preview-1201558104/|url-status=live}}</ref> Ticket selling website [[Fandango (ticket service)|Fandango]] reported that the film was outselling ''Gravity''.<ref name="track2" /> Unlike ''Gravity'', ''The Martian'' did not contain abundant 3D spectacle (even though it was filmed in 3D), and was longer than ''Gravity''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/news/?id=4109 |title=Forecast: Can 'The Martian' Top 'Gravity's October Record? |first=Brad |last=Brevet |work=[[Box Office Mojo]] |date=October 1, 2015 |access-date=October 2, 2015 |archive-date=October 2, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151002223849/http://www.boxofficemojo.com/news/?id=4109 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Theatrical run===
''The Martian'' was a financial success.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2016/film/news/21st-century-fox-earnings-cable-gains-cant-lift-weaker-film-results-1201700127/|title=21st Century Fox Earnings: Cable Gains Can't Lift Weaker Film Results|first=Brent|last=Lang|work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|date=February 8, 2016|access-date=February 9, 2016|archive-date=February 9, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160209094631/https://variety.com/2016/film/news/21st-century-fox-earnings-cable-gains-cant-lift-weaker-film-results-1201700127/|url-status=live}}</ref> It grossed $228.4&nbsp;million in the United States & Canada and $425.2&nbsp;million in other countries, for a worldwide total of $653.6&nbsp;million against a budget of $108&nbsp;million.<ref name="BOM" /> Worldwide, it was the [[2015 in film#Highest-grossing films|tenth-highest-grossing film of 2015]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2015 Worldwide Box Office |url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/world/2015/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200818152249/https://www.boxofficemojo.com/year/world/2015/ |archive-date=August 18, 2020 |access-date=June 30, 2023 |website=[[Box Office Mojo]]}}</ref> ''[[Deadline Hollywood]]'' calculated the net profit of the film to be $150.32&nbsp;million, accounting for production budgets, P&A, talent participations, and other costs, with box office grosses, and ancillary revenues from home media, placing it tenth on their list of 2015's "Most Valuable Blockbusters";<ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2016/03/the-martian-2015-profit-box-office-2015-matt-damon-ridley-scott-1201724168/|title=No. 10 'The Martian' – 2015 Most Valuable Movie Blockbuster Tournament|first=Mike Jr.|last=Fleming|work=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|date=March 23, 2016|access-date=March 24, 2016|archive-date=March 24, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160324191127/http://deadline.com/2016/03/the-martian-2015-profit-box-office-2015-matt-damon-ridley-scott-1201724168/|url-status=live}}</ref> and ''[[The Hollywood Reporter]]'' reported around $80–100&nbsp;million profits for the film.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/oscar-profitability-goes-martian-872507|title=And the Oscar for Profitability Goes to ... 'The Martian'|first=Pamela|last=McClintock|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|date=March 3, 2016|access-date=September 14, 2016|archive-date=October 12, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161012024433/http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/oscar-profitability-goes-martian-872507|url-status=live}}</ref>

The film was released in theaters in 2D and 3D.<ref name="lang">{{cite journal | last=Lang | first=Brent | url=https://variety.com/2015/film/box-office/3d-the-walk-the-martian-reald-1201538750/ | title=Movies Like 'The Martian,' 'The Walk' Will Be Important for 3D, Says RealD Chief | journal=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] | date=July 12, 2015 | access-date=August 26, 2015 | archive-date=August 23, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150823041047/http://variety.com/2015/film/box-office/3d-the-walk-the-martian-reald-1201538750/ | url-status=live }}</ref> In the United Kingdom, it was released on September 30, 2015, a Wednesday,<ref>{{cite news | last=De Semlyen | first=Phil | url=https://www.empireonline.com/news/story.asp?NID=45206 | title=Exclusive New Look At Ridley Scott's The Martian | work=[[Empire (magazine)|Empire]] | date=August 25, 2015 | access-date=August 28, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150905104623/http://www.empireonline.com/news/story.asp?NID=45206 |archive-date=September 5, 2015}}</ref> and in the United States on the following Friday, October 2, 2015.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=McClintock | first1=Pamela | last2=Ford | first2=Rebecca | url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/box-office-martian-rocketing-powerful-828685 | title=Box Office: 'The Martian' Rocketing to Powerful $48M-$50M Debut | journal=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] | date=October 2, 2015 | access-date=October 2, 2015 | archive-date=October 2, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151002221210/http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/box-office-martian-rocketing-powerful-828685 | url-status=live }}</ref> It was also released in 49 markets including Mexico, Hong Kong, India and Taiwan from the weekend October 2–4, 2015 and expanded to Germany, Russia, and South Korea the following weekend. It opened in Spain on October 16, then France on October 21. China opened on November 25 and Japan bowed in the first quarter of 2016 on February 5.<ref name="Overseas10thOpening"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2015/film/news/matt-damon-the-martian-china-release-nov-25-1201624520/|title=Matt Damon's 'The Martian' Set for China Release on Nov. 25|first=Dave|last=McNary|author-link=Dave McNary|work=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]|date=October 22, 2015|access-date=October 23, 2015|archive-date=October 23, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151023205849/http://variety.com/2015/film/news/matt-damon-the-martian-china-release-nov-25-1201624520/|url-status=live}}</ref> Various sites estimated the film to gross between $45 and $50&nbsp;million over its opening weekend in the United States.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.boxofficemojo.com/news/?id=4109&p=.htm|title=Forecast: Can 'The Martian' Top 'Gravity's October Record?|first=Bred|last=Brevet|work=Box Office Mojo|publisher=[[Amazon.com]]|date=October 1, 2015|access-date=October 3, 2015|archive-date=October 4, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151004011047/http://www.boxofficemojo.com/news/?id=4109&p=.htm|url-status=live}}</ref>

In North America, it opened on Friday, October 2, 2015, and earned $18.06&nbsp;million on its opening day of which $2&nbsp;million came from premium large formats from 3,831 theaters.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://deadline.com/2015/10/the-martian-the-walk-sicario-weekend-box-office-1201565765/|title='The Martian' Defies 'Gravity' On Friday; 'Everest' & 'The Walk' In Large Format Quandary – Saturday AM Box Office Update|first=Anthony|last=D'Alessandro|work=[[Deadline Hollywood]]|date=October 3, 2015|access-date=October 4, 2015|archive-date=June 16, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180616030854/https://deadline.com/2015/10/the-martian-the-walk-sicario-weekend-box-office-1201565765/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite For its United States release, the film was originally scheduled to be released on November 25, 2015, but 20th Century Fox switched ''The Martian'' with ''[[Victor Frankenstein (film)|Victor Frankenstein]]'' so that the former would be its first film for all audiences in the country's fall season (September–November).<ref name="mcclintock">{{cite journal | last=McClintock | first=Pamela | url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/fox-moves-ridley-scotts-martian-801733 | title=Fox Moves Ridley Scott's 'The Martian' to October | journal=[[The Hollywood Reporter]] | date=June 10, 2015 | access-date=August 26, 2015 | archive-date=August 23, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150823161700/http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/fox-moves-ridley-scotts-martian-801733 | url-status=live }}</ref> On the film's 3D screenings, RealD's chief Anthony Marcoly said 3D technology was proliferating from action-packed [[blockbuster (entertainment)|blockbuster]] films commonly released in the United States' summer season. Marcoly said the technology was being used in more immersive storytelling, citing ''The Martian'' and ''[[The Walk (2015 film)|The Walk]]'' (released the same year) as two examples.<ref name="lang" />

===Home media===
''The Martian'' was released on Digital on December 22, 2015 {{Citation needed|reason=The current ref on this section appears to only list the extended cut 2016 release |date=June 2023}} and on [[Blu-ray]] and DVD on January 12, 2016. It was released on 4K Ultra HD Blu-ray on February 14, 2016. An extended cut of the film adding an additional ten minutes was released on June 7, 2016.<ref name="Collider"/>

==Reception==

===Critical response===
{{Anchor|Critics|Reception}}
On the [[review aggregator]] [[Rotten Tomatoes]], {{RT data|score}} of {{RT data|count}} critics gave the film a positive review and the average rating was {{RT data|average}}. The website's critics consensus read, "Smart, thrilling, and surprisingly funny, ''The Martian'' offers a faithful adaptation of the bestselling book that brings out the best in leading man Matt Damon and director Ridley Scott."<ref>{{Cite Rotten Tomatoes |id={{RT data|rtid|noprefix=y}} |type=m |title=The Martian |access-date={{RT data|access date}}}}{{cbignore}}</ref> [[Metacritic]], which uses a weighted average, assigned the film a score of 80 out of 100 based on 46 critics indicating "generally favorable" reviews.<ref>{{cite Metacritic |id=the-martian|type=movie|title=The Martian|access-date=February 19, 2021}}</ref> Audiences polled by [[CinemaScore]] gave the film an average grade of "A" on an A+ to F scale, while [[PostTrak]] reported filmgoers gave it an average 4.5 out of 5 and a 66% "definite recommend". Audience demographics were 54% men and a total of 59% over 35.<ref>{{cite web |last=D'Alessandro |first=Anthony |title='Martian' 2nd-Best Opening For October, Damon & Scott Despite Losing Fuel Sunday; Verdi Trips 'Walk' – B.O. Postmortem |url=https://deadline.com/2015/10/the-martian-the-walk-sicario-weekend-box-office-1201565765/ |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |date=October 6, 2015 |access-date=June 26, 2016 |archive-date=June 16, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180616030854/https://deadline.com/2015/10/the-martian-the-walk-sicario-weekend-box-office-1201565765/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

According to Rotten Tomatoes, critics said that the film "finds Scott examining more hopeful territory, and the result is an awe-inspiring adventure that explores vast ideas while staying grounded in very human emotional territory. [...] ''The Martian'' is visually stunning, scientifically credible, and immensely likable, thanks in large part to Damon's funny, touching performance."<!-- Per WP:PEACOCK: Avoid terms like "acclaim" that promote the subject without attribution --><ref>{{cite web | last=Ryan | first=Tim | url=https://editorial.rottentomatoes.com/article/the-martian/ | title=The Martian is Certified Fresh | publisher=[[Fandango Media]] | work=[[Rotten Tomatoes]] | date=October 1, 2015 | access-date=October 2, 2015 | archive-date=October 3, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151003021148/http://editorial.rottentomatoes.com/article/the-martian/ | url-status=live }}</ref> ''[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]]'' reported, "Critics are calling the film a funny, thrilling ride, and a return to form for [Ridley] Scott after ''[[The Counselor]]'' and ''[[Exodus: Gods and Kings]]'' fell flat."<ref>{{cite journal | last=Lang | first=Brent | url=https://variety.com/2015/film/news/the-martian-box-office-matt-damon-1201605217/ | title=Box Office: 'The Martian' to Blast Off With $45 Million | journal=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] | date=September 29, 2015 | access-date=September 30, 2015 | archive-date=September 30, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150930234237/http://variety.com/2015/film/news/the-martian-box-office-matt-damon-1201605217/ | url-status=live }}</ref> In ''[[The Guardian]]'', aerospace engineer [[Robert Zubrin]] commented:  {{cquote|[The film] is the first genuine Mars movie. It is the first movie that attempts to be realistic and that is actually about human beings grappling with the problems of exploring Mars, as opposed to various movies set on Mars that are essentially either shoot'em ups or horror films. It does not engage in fantasy: no monsters, no magic, no Nazis. However, there are a number of technical mistakes.<ref name="TG-20151006-rz">{{cite news |last=Zubrin |first=Robert |author-link=Robert Zubrin |title=How scientifically accurate is The Martian? |url=https://www.theguardian.com/film/2015/oct/06/how-scientifically-accurate-is-the-martian |date=October 6, 2015 |work=[[The Guardian]] |access-date=October 7, 2015 |archive-date=October 8, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151008222115/http://www.theguardian.com/film/2015/oct/06/how-scientifically-accurate-is-the-martian |url-status=live }}</ref>}}

[[Manohla Dargis]], of ''[[The New York Times]]'', stated that the film "involves a dual journey into outer and inner space, a trip that takes you into that immensity called the universe and deep into the equally vast landscape of a single consciousness. For this accidental castaway, space is the place where he's physically marooned, but also where his mind is set free", from a film director, whose "great, persistent theme is what it means to be human".<ref name="NYT-20151001">{{cite news |last=Dargis |first=Manohla |title=Review: In 'The Martian,' Marooned but Not Alone |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2015/10/02/movies/review-in-the-martian-marooned-but-not-alone.html |date=October 1, 2015 |work=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=October 2, 2015 |archive-date=October 2, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151002135328/http://www.nytimes.com/2015/10/02/movies/review-in-the-martian-marooned-but-not-alone.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

Negative reviews focused on the lack of character depth or atmosphere. Jaime N. Christley, writing in ''[[Slant Magazine]]'', commented, "It goes in for the idea of texture, tics, and human behavior, but there's no conviction, and no real push for eccentricity. ... It hardly seems interested in its characters or in any depiction of their work, settling instead for types of characters and kinds of scenes, correctly placed among the pendulum swings of Watney's dramatic journey."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.slantmagazine.com/film/review/the-martian |title=The Martian |last=Christley |first=Jaime |work=[[Slant Magazine]] |date=September 23, 2015 |access-date=August 15, 2016 |archive-date=May 29, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160529040053/http://www.slantmagazine.com/film/review/the-martian |url-status=live }}</ref> In ''[[The Village Voice]]'', [[Stephanie Zacharek]] stated that the actors "are treated as accessories", and that the director is "workmanlike in his approach to science, which always trumps magic in ''The Martian''—that's the point. But if we can't feel a sense of wonder at the magnitude and mystery of space, why even bother?"<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.villagevoice.com/film/life-finds-a-way-damon-s-got-more-spirit-in-him-than-the-martian-itself-does-7703991 |title=Life Finds a Way: Damon's Got More Spirit in Him Than 'The Martian' Itself Does |last=Zacharek |first=Stephanie |work=[[The Village Voice]] |date=September 25, 2015 |access-date=August 15, 2016 |archive-date=September 15, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160915134632/http://www.villagevoice.com/film/life-finds-a-way-damon-s-got-more-spirit-in-him-than-the-martian-itself-does-7703991 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In ''Cinemixtape'', J. Olson commented: "Ridley Scott and company have concocted the most colossally mediocre sci-fi movie of the decade, all in pursuit of empty backslapping and a grade school level celebration of science. Not only is ''The Martian'' not in the same class as Scott's two masterpieces – ''[[Alien (film)|Alien]]'' and ''[[Blade Runner]]'' – it's not even on the same continent."<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cinemixtape.com/movie-reviews/martian/ |title="The Martian" Is Handsome, Hollow Sci-Fi |last=Olson |first=J. |work=Cinemixtape |access-date=August 15, 2016 |date=October 11, 2015 |archive-date=August 21, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160821010941/http://www.cinemixtape.com/movie-reviews/martian/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
